items.title: Former Congress ally Gogoi tells Rahul Gandhi his parallel protests have weakened independent CJP mass movement
points: Mr. Gogoi said the Congress had weakened the movement by competing with what he described was “a genuine mass revolt”, thereby dividing the Opposition’s street mobilisation.

He also expressed concern over Mr. Gandhi’s silence on two earlier letters (dated October 29 and November 12, respectively), in which he sought clarity on the Congress’s approach to the movement and the Opposition’s strategy for the 2029 Lok Sabha election.

“As someone who has spent his entire life on the streets fighting alongside peasants, workers, and the masses — not inside air-conditioned rooms — your continued silence troubles me deeply,” Mr. Gogoi wrote.

He described the CJP agitation as the most effective people’s movement against the BJP-RSS government, claiming that it had mobilised the youth within five months in a manner that traditional Opposition politics had failed to achieve over the past 12 years.
Mr. Gogoi asked Mr. Gandhi to explain why the Congress had undermined the movement and what its position was on supporting an independent mass struggle.

items.title: SC upholds stay on Azam Khan’s conviction in fake birth certificate case, extends relief to wife, son
points: The Supreme Court of India in New Delhi. | Photo Credit: File The Supreme Court on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) upheld the Allahabad High Court’s decision to stay the conviction of Samajwadi Party leader Mohammed Azam Khan in a case involving allegedly…
The court also stayed the convictions of Mr. Khan’s wife, Dr. Tazeen Fatma, and son in the same case.

A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu dismissed appeals filed by the Uttar Pradesh government against the High Court’s May 24, 2024, decision, while allowing separate appeals filed by Mr. Khan’s wife and son.

“Though differential treatment is not forbidden, an unreasoned differential treatment cannot be sustained,” the Bench observed, holding that the High Court had failed to justify why Mr. Khan’s wife and son were denied the same relief despite being…
The Bench held that the High Court’s refusal to extend the stay of conviction to Mr. Khan’s wife and son violated the doctrine of parity and amounted to a jurisdictional error.

items.title: Rajnath Singh to visit Japan for Ministerial dialogue on defence cooperation
points: According to the Ministry of Defence, the 2+2 Ministerial Dialogue, scheduled to be held in Tokyo, will be co-chaired by Mr. Singh and External Affairs Minister S.
Jaishankar, along with Japan’s Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi.
The dialogue is expected to review the entire spectrum of bilateral strategic and defence cooperation, besides providing an opportunity to exchange views on regional and global developments.
The two sides will also reaffirm their commitment to a free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific, it added.
The two Ministers had earlier met in New Delhi in August and on the sidelines of the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus in Cebu in October.

During the upcoming discussions, the two sides are expected to deliberate on expanding defence equipment and technology collaboration, strengthening maritime security, enhancing the scale and complexity of joint military exercises across all three services…
India and Japan share a Special Strategic and Global Partnership founded on shared democratic values, mutual trust and converging strategic interests.

items.title: Nearly 75 lakh names added in draft SSR voters lists in 13 States and UTs
points: The SSR, on hold since the SIR process began last year, was first announced in 17 States and UTs, including poll-bound Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Punjab, on October 15.

ALLEN EGENUSE Months after final voters lists were published following the contentious special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, nearly 75 lakh more names have been added in draft voter lists published in 13 States and Union Territories via a…
The combined size of the electorate in these States before the SIR was 49.61 crore, which shrunk to 45.22 crore after the SIR and has now increased to 45.96 crore in the draft SSR list.
Uttar Pradesh, which published its draft SSR list on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), saw 18.84 lakh names being added to its voter lists, the largest in absolute numbers so far.
Bihar, which was the first State to undergo the SIR process in 2025 saw 13.89 lakh names being added to the final post-SIR list.

The Nifty rose 0.4% to end at 25,387.40, while the Sensex gained 0.5%.
Foreign investors have put about $10 billion into Indian stocks this month.
The Nifty Bank closed 1.1% higher, hitting an all-time high on Tuesday, while the Nifty IT ended 0.9% lower.
According to provisional data, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) were net buyers of Indian equities worth ₹4,195 crore on Tuesday.
Nifty companies delivered 27% year-on-year profit growth in the September quarter, yet brokerages raised their FY27 and FY28 earnings estimates by only 0.9% and 1.4%, respectively.

The benchmark Nifty 50 has gained 10% this month, the best performance among major Asian markets, according to Bloomberg data.Major global indices, including the Nasdaq (-2.5%), S&P 500 (-1.9%), Dow Jones (-1.4%), DAX (-0.5%), Hang Seng (-0.8%), Nikkei…
Failure to break above that level could lead to an extended consolidation in the 25,000-25,500 range, said Pabitro Mukherjee, deputy vice-president, research, Bajaj Broking.

The inaugural session will be held at PVP Siddhartha College of Information Technology, while the subsequent sessions over the three days will be conducted at P.B.

items.title: Naidu seeks immediate Central assistance to cope with damages caused by two cyclones
points: Chandrababu Naidu with Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in New Delhi on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: ANI Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N.

Chandrababu Naidu has sought immediate financial assistance from the Union government to help the State cope with the damage caused by two successive cyclones (Arnab and Murasu), which inflicted losses estimated at over ₹7,000 crore.

During a meeting with Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in New Delhi on November 17, 2026 (Tuesday), Mr. Naidu explained the impact of the two cyclones on agriculture, power infrastructure and other sectors, and urged her to extend immediate…
He said crops nearing harvest had been damaged, leaving farmers in distress.

Despite the impact of El Niño, the State had supplied irrigation water to some regions through the Pattiseema project to help the farmers, but the successive cyclones caused extensive crop losses, the Chief Minister said.
The Chief Minister said Central teams had visited the State to assess the damage and were expected to submit their reports soon.

items.title: Four Assam villages to convert grazing land into community reserve forest
points: Image for the purpose of representation. | Photo Credit: File Four villages in northeastern Assam’s Dhemaji district have come together to convert 1,044 bighas (about 345 acres) of shared grazing land into a community reserve forest.
They intend to offer a safe habitat for some 150 deer vulnerable to poaching in the jungles beyond the grazing land.

“This is a positive development for wildlife protection,” Assam Environment and Forest Minister Jayanta Mallabaruah said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), lauding the community-led conservation initiative.
The four villages (Gohain Chapori, Hator Khola, Puthimari and No. 1 Barmuthoni) share the Maghuwa Hola grazing ground for their livestock.
Earlier, Mr. Mallabaruah highlighted the restoration of degraded forest land in Biswanath district’s Behali Wildlife Sanctuary with 1.25 lakh native saplings.

Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma praised the 134 Infantry Battalion (Territorial Army) Ecological Task Force for its role in afforestation and wildlife conservation in Behali near the Assam-Arunachal Pradesh border.
“Behali Wildlife Sanctuary is an important part of Assam’s natural landscape.

items.title: Keralam to inform HC on tourist bus colour change
points: Updated - November 17, 2026 09:21 pm IST - THIRUVANANTHAPURAM The State government will inform the High Court on November 19 of its decision to modify the uniform white colour scheme mandated for tourist buses in Keralam.

The decision was taken at a meeting of the State Transport Authority (STA) held here on Tuesday, following an interim order of the High Court and after taking into account the views of bus owners and other stakeholders.
The uniform white colour scheme for tourist buses was strictly enforced in the State following the Vadakkencherry bus accident in Palakkad in 2022.

However, bus owners have complained that the regulation has pushed the State’s tourist bus sector into a severe crisis, as buses from other States operating under All India Permits are not subject to similar restrictions.
This has put vehicles registered in Keralam at a competitive disadvantage, affecting their business and the livelihoods of thousands of workers.

items.title: Minister calls for unity among alliance leaders to ensure victory in panchayat polls
points: Janardhan Reddy has expressed confidence that the candidates supported by the NDA will certainly achieve a resounding victory in the upcoming panchayat elections.
Continuing his discussions with the leaders of NDA partners ahead of the sarpanch elections, Mr. Janardhan Reddy on Tuesday held meeting with the leaders from Owk and Banaganapalle mandals.
During the discussions, he highlighted that the public had faith in the alliance government, and with their blessings, would continue their winning streak at the village level as well.

During the meeting, discussions were also held regarding the political landscape in each village of the mandal, election preparedness, the selection of candidates, and coordination among the alliance parties.
The Minister noted that the alliance government, under the leadership of Chief Minister N.
He added that the positive sentiment among the public on the government’s performance would be reflected in the panchayat elections.
He urged the leaders of the alliance parties at the village level to work in coordination, setting aside personal differences.

items.title: Cyclone Akvan moves slowly, likely to intensify further by November 18 morning
points: Fishing boats remain anchored to the shore at Jalaripeta in Visakhapatnam on Tuesday, as Andhra Pradesh braces for Cyclone Akvan. | Photo Credit: K.R.
DEEPAK Cyclonic storm Akvan (meaning ‘demon’ in Persian) over the central parts of the south and west-central Bay of Bengal may intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by Wednesday morning.

Initially, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast that the weather system would strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening, but the system had either remained stationary or moved slowly.

At 5.30 p.m., the weather system was centred around 590 km east of Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 630 km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, 650 km southeast of Machilipatnam and 650 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and 780 km south of…

It may continue to move slowly north-northwestwards and intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over west-central Bay of Bengal on Wednesday morning, and further into a very severe cyclonic storm by Thursday morning.

items.title: Assam’s Karbi Anglong sets Guinness record with 15,000 dancers
points: Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council chief Tuliram Ronghang greets dancers after 15,000 of them set a Guinness World Record on Tuesday night.

About 15,000 dancers representing different communities of Assam’s Karbi Anglong district set a Guinness World Record on Monday evening (November 17, 2026), the second such feat for folk music and dance in the northeastern region within a week.
Garo community drummers in Meghalaya set a world record on November 14 by playing 1,000 damas (elongated drums) during the Wangala Festival in Tura, the State’s second-largest urban centre.

Karbi Anglong has made its mark on the world stage!” Tuliram Ronghang, the Chief Executive Member of the Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council (KAAC) said in a social media post after an official adjudicator of Guinness World Records announced the achievement.
The record was set at the Karbi Anglong Sports Association Stadium in Diphu, about 250 km east of Guwahati, during the district’s 75th anniversary celebrations organised by the KAAC.

items.title: Some Congress leaders stalled probe into Modi in Gujarat riots case, claims Veerappa Moily
points: Former Chief Minister and former Union Minister M.

Veerappa Moily on Tuesday alleged that some Congress leaders in the then UPA government had stalled the investigation into Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the alleged 2002 Gujarat riots case when he was the Chief Minister of the State.
Speaking after releasing Sonia Gandhi’s book Belonging – A Journey of Love at the KPCC office in Bengaluru, Mr. Moily said, “Home Minister Amit Shah was the first one to go to jail.
His case was tried outside Gujarat, and he was living in exile.” Mr. Shah was arrested by the CBI in 2010 in connection with the alleged Sohrabuddin Sheikh fake encounter case.
In December 2014, a special court in Mumbai discharged him, citing lack of evidence.
Mr. Moily was the Union Law Minister during 2010-11.
Following a Supreme Court directive in 2009, a Special Investigation Team (SIT) questioned Mr. Modi in 2010 regarding an alleged larger conspiracy during the 2002 riots.

items.title: Karnataka has a ‘goonda government’, says Ashok
points: Alleging a rise in “goondaism” in the State after D.K.
Shivakumar became Chief Minister, Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly R.
Ashok on Tuesday claimed that BJP workers active on social media were being targeted by the police through the registration of false cases.

Kote, Mr. Ashok said BJP activists on social media in different parts of the State, including Bidar, Kalaburagi and Bagalkot, were being summoned by the police and forced to furnish bonds of ₹5 lakh for expressing their views.
After Mr. Shivakumar assumed office as Chief Minister, the State appeared to be under an “indirect Emergency”, he said, adding that it looked like Karnataka had a “goonda government”.

Criticising Mr. Shivakumar for “spending most of his time in Delhi”, Mr. Ashok said the Chief Minister had no concern for farmers in distress owing to drought and alleged that farmer suicides in the State had increased.

items.title: 45-year-old scrap dealer shot dead in a parked car near Madanayakanahalli
points: The police suspect that someone known to the victim may have carried out the murder. | Photo Credit: Getty Images A 45-year-old scrap businessman was shot dead inside a parked car in Manchepanahalli under the Bagaluru Police Station limits on Sunday afternoon.
The deceased has been identified as Imraz Pasha, a resident of Bannerghatta.
According to the police, Imraz Pasha had left his home in a car on Sunday afternoon to meet an acquaintance to discuss a business-related matter.
Passersby later noticed Imraz Pasha lying dead inside a car parked near a private layout in Manchepanahalli and alerted the police.
Preliminary investigation revealed that Imraz Pasha had been shot with a pistol.
Joint Commissioner of Police (East Division) Ramesh Bannoth visited the spot and supervised the investigation.
His son Rizwan Pasha told the media that he was with his father at the business site in Yelahanka when his father received a call from an old friend, Naveed Baig.

items.title: SEBI revises minimum margin norms for commodity derivatives
points: The new margin norms are set to come into effect from December 1.

Markets regulator SEBI on Tuesday revised the minimum initial margin and minimum Margin Period of Risk (MPOR) requirements for the commodity derivatives segment, with the new norms set to come into effect from December 1.

Under the revised framework, the minimum initial margin for low-volatility commodities has been fixed at 6 per cent, and the requirement for medium- and high-volatility commodities will be 8 per cent and 10 per cent, respectively, according to a SEBI circular.
The revised requirements will apply uniformly to agricultural and non-agricultural commodities.
SEBI has also prescribed a minimum MPOR of two days for low- and medium-volatility commodities and three days for high-volatility commodities across both categories.

The changes follow representations from market stakeholders and recommendations from a working group on the review of regulatory norms applicable to the agricultural commodity derivatives segment and the Risk Management Review Committee (RMRC).

items.title: India records nearly 80% decline in malaria cases and deaths from 2015 to 2025: President
points: The President highlighted India’s progress in malaria control, noting that malaria cases and deaths had declined by nearly 80% between 2015 and 2025, while the number of high-burden districts fell from 155 to 33.
She also noted that 160 districts reported zero indigenous malaria cases during 2022-2025.

Appreciating India’s exit from the World Health Organization’s (WHO) High Burden to High Impact (HBHI) group in 2024, she acknowledged the collective efforts of scientists, healthcare workers and citizens.

Emphasising the need for continued vigilance and effective interventions, the President called for strengthened malaria diagnosis, treatment and surveillance, mosquito control, development of new medicines and vaccines, greater public awareness and…

She also expressed satisfaction over ICMR-NIMR’s contribution to the indigenous malaria vaccine being developed in Bhubaneswar, and voiced confidence that it would support India’s malaria elimination efforts.
The President also released a commemorative postage stamp sheet marking the Golden Jubilee of the institute, following its introduction by Mariamma Thomas, Member, Postal Services Board.

items.title: IAF mobile publicity vehicle traversing Karnataka

The publicity vehicle, which was flagged off on Tuesday (November 17) from Head Quarter Training Command, will cover approximately 60 km daily to reach the youth of various districts.
The drive will traverse through Ramanagara, Mandya, Mysuru, Piriyapatna, Madikeri and Sullia, culminating at Bantwal on November 23.
To engage the youth, the team will conduct interactive sessions and games at various educational institutions.

The scheduled stops include Bidadi (November 17), Channapatna (November 18), Srirangapatna (November 19), Piriyapatna (November 20), Kushalnagar (November 21), Sullia (November 22), Puttur and Bantwal (November 23).

Ananth, Senior Officer-in-charge Administration, HQ Training Command, who flagged off the vehicle, highlighted the adventurous and patriotic lifestyle offered by the IAF and encouraged the youth to embrace the challenge and consider a distinguished career…

items.title: Art to find a place in every panchayat’s annual plan: Minister
points: Vishnunadh with winners of Kerala Sangeetha Nataka Akademi Fellowships, the Akademi’s highest honour for lifetime contributions to the arts - theatre director and playwright Jayaprakash Kuloor, music director and lyricist Kaithapram Damodaran Namboothiri,…
Venu - in Thrissur on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: K.

NAJEEB The State government will work towards earmarking funds in the annual plans of all local self-government institutions to promote dance, drama, music and other art forms, Cultural Affairs Minister P.C.

Speaking after presenting the Kerala Sangeetha Nataka Akademi’s awards for 2025, in Thrissur on Tuesday, the Minister said the government would seek changes in the existing cultural policy to ensure that cultural activities were not confined to urban centres.
The government would also seek a higher allocation for the Cultural Affairs Department in the State Budget to strengthen cultural initiatives across Kerala, he added.
The Minister presented fellowships to three eminent artistes, awards to 18 persons and Gurupuja awards to 22 recipients for their contributions to different fields of art.

items.title: Maharashtra FDA shuts businesses of five food outlets, suspends four licences over norm violations
points: Stepping up its enforcement drive, the Maharashtra FDA has served 'stop business' notices on five food establishments, suspended four licences and seized food stock worth over Rs 1.97 crore during inspections carried out across the state, officials said on…

The latest Food and Drug Administration (FDA) action covered establishments in Pune, Mumbai, Thane, Palghar and Nagpur districts, among others, over alleged violations of safety norms and hygiene lapses.

The FDA seized 97,578 kg of wet dates and cinnamon worth ₹1.11 crore from a godown operated by Shri Sadhak Stockage (Fresh Max) in Navi Mumbai's Koparkhairane area over suspected mislabelling and substandard quality, said the officials.
In Palghar, officials seized 59,496 kg of unlabelled areca nuts (supari) worth ₹68.71 lakh from two trucks parked along the Mumbai-Ahmedabad highway.

In Mumbai, the food safety authority seized dietary supplement products worth ₹5.59 lakh containing nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), a prohibited ingredient, from Rahul Distributors and Amritlal and Brothers, they said.

items.title: Women to make up 30% of Kerala Police force: Chennithala
points: Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala with the newly inducted Sub-Inspectors after the passing-out parade of the 32nd batch at the Kerala Police Academy, Ramavarmapuram, on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: K.K.
NAJEEB The State government has taken a historic decision to gradually increase women’s representation in the Kerala Police to 30%, Home and Vigilance Minister Ramesh Chennithala has said.

He was addressing the passing-out parade of the 32-B batch of Sub-Inspectors at the Kerala Police Academy, Ramavarmapuram, on Tuesday after receiving the salute from the 89 officers who completed their one-year training programme.
The Minister said women officers were performing on a par with their male counterparts in terms of hard work, dedication and crime detection.
At present, women officers are serving as Station House Officers (SHOs) in 63 police stations across the State, he said.

items.title: Jefferies sees limited impact on MTF curbs
points: Jefferies’ analysis shows the proposed restrictions would have a sharply different impact depending on where the cap is set.

At 10 per cent of free float, only 4 per cent of the current MTF book would be affected India’s markets regulator is considering capping margin-funded purchases at 5–10 per cent of a stock’s free float, a move that analysts at Jefferies say poses only…
According to a Reuters report on Tuesday, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is weighing the curbs amid concerns over concentrated leverage in select stocks.

India’s margin trading facility (MTF) book has grown to ₹1.5 trillion, roughly doubling over the past two years, driven by the tightening of index options rules and the rise of discount broking platforms offering margin lending.
At 10 per cent of free float, only 4 per cent of the current MTF book would be affected.
A tighter 5 per cent cap, however, would bring 23 per cent of the book into scope.

items.title: HDK hopeful of alliance partners fielding consensus NDA candidate for Hiriyur bypolls
points: Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel H.D.
Kumaraswamy has expressed confidence that the JD(S) and BJP will arrive at a consensus while deciding on the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) candidate for the Hiriyur Assembly byelection.

Speaking to reporters at Mysuru airport on Tuesday, Mr. Kumaraswamy acknowledged that JD(S) workers were demanding that the party field a candidate, while BJP workers were making a similar demand for their party.
He said neither demand was unreasonable and added that leaders of the two alliance partners would sit together and arrive at a consensus.
“The common objective of the alliance partners is to defeat the Congress candidate,” he said, emphasising that there would be no prestige issue in this regard.
The situation in the constituency was favourable for the victory of the NDA candidate, he said, adding that there was a strong anti-incumbency wave against the Congress in the State.

items.title: Opposition questions Supreme Court order in Bilkis Bano case
points: Bilkis Bano in a statement, expressed shock at the SC order, saying she had not been informed about the proceedings.

File | Photo Credit: Thulasi Kakkat The Opposition leaders on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) questioned the suspension of sentences of two convicts in the Bilkis Bano case, with the Congress saying the rape survivor was being made to endure “fresh humiliation…
Varale had granted bail to Bipin Chandra Joshi and Pradeep Mordhiya, noting that they had spent more than 17 years in prison and that their appeals raised questions of fact and law.
The two, who were serving life imprisonment, were among the 11 convicts whose remission was quashed by the Supreme Court in 2024.
Congress media and publicity department head Pawan Khera said Ms. Bano had learnt about the court’s decision through media reports and was not heard before the order was passed.
Baby termed the Supreme Court order “shocking and reprehensible”.

items.title: State power utilities working towards uninterrupted power supply during Rabi, summer
points: Complimenting the officials for ensuring trouble free power supply during the Kharif season not just to the agriculture sector but to all other categories of consumers too.

Despite a 4,000 MW hydel power generation shortfall on account of the poor rainy season, the Deputy Chief Minister asked the officials to be prepared for the coming months to ensure interruption-free power supply during the Rabi season too.

Officials of the energy department and Southern Discom informed the Deputy Chief Minister that augmentation of power supply infrastructure was also continuing and two newly built 33/11 kV substations at Dawoodkhan Guda and Badangpet were charged.
They would not only help meet the growing demand in the Saroornagar Circle but also improve supply reliability.

Cautioning officials on the possibilities of days when power demand might spike during the Rabi season, the Deputy Chief Minister told them to continuously monitor the demand and ensure uninterrupted power supply to all categories of consumers.

items.title: HPV-DNA testing to be implemented in five high-burden districts of T.N.
points: The Health Department plans to cover 1,24,215 women under the HPV-DNA testing programme.
Tamil Nadu is all set to implement HPV-DNA testing for cervical cancer in the five high-burden districts of Dharmapuri, Villupuram, Tiruvannamalai, Perambalur and Ariyalur in the first phase.
The Health department plans to cover 1,24,215 women under the HPV-DNA testing programme.
According to the Tamil Nadu Cancer Registry Project 2023 report, 87,156 new cancer cases - 37,931 among men and 49,225 among women - were reported in Tamil Nadu in 2023.
The projected number of new cancer cases for 2026 is around one lakh (94,098), it said.

The WHO Regional Implementation Framework for elimination of cervical cancer emphasising the 90-70-90 targets, includes screening of 70% of women with a high-performance test by 35 years of age and again by 45 years of age.

items.title: OU students protest poor-quality meals
points: Students of the ladies’ hostel at Osmania University staged a protest late on Monday over the alleged supply of poor-quality and unhygienic food.
Around 100 women students pursuing MBA and Law courses participated in the protest, raising concerns over the quality of food served at the hostel.
The students alleged that they had found worms in the rice served to them.
To substantiate their claims, they took to the streets carrying plates and bowls containing rice and curries.
The students expressed dissatisfaction over the hostel management’s response, and stated that repeated complaints about food quality had gone unaddressed.

They also pointed to previous incidents of contaminated and poor-quality food at the university, in which blades and worms were allegedly found in food, and curries were served uncooked or were too watery.
Later, the police at OU station reached the protest site and spoke to the students.

items.title: Skilled-worker shortage pushes up cyclone repair costs in coastal Andhra
points: Workers carrying out repairs to a house damaged by Cyclones Arnab and Murasu in West Godavari district.

Construction workers are in high demand in parts of Eluru, West Godavari and Krishna districts as residents take up repair works on houses damaged by strong winds and heavy rain during Cyclones Arnab and Murasu.
The damage has triggered a surge in demand for skilled workers, leading to a shortage of masons, plumbers, electricians and other technicians, residents of Kaikalur in Eluru district said.
Trees, coconut palms and electricity poles fell on houses in Mudinepalli, Bhimavaram, Veeravasaram, Palakollu, Narsapuram and other places.
Though masons, plumbers, electricians and water motor mechanics had been attending to repair works for the past 10 days, normalcy was yet to be restored, said Annapurna, a resident of Tadepalligudem.
“There is a shortage of skilled workers.
The estimated damage to individual households ranged from ₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh.

items.title: Italian tourist found dead in Manali hotel
points: An Italian tourist was found dead under suspicious circumstances in his hotel room at Chanala-Jagatsukh near Manali in Himachal Pradesh, police said on Tuesday.
According to the police, Faraday Michael did not step out of his room for about a day.
Suspecting something had gone wrong, the hotel management informed the Manali police station on Tuesday.
When police opened the room, they found Michael lying dead on the bed with no injury marks on his body, officials said.
His passport, cash, a mobile phone and some medicines were found in the room.
Michael was a heavy smoker, and it is believed that he was suffering from asthma, police said.
Police have informed the Italian Embassy in Delhi about the incident after sending the body to a mortuary in Manali.
Further action will be taken as per rules, they said.

items.title: Rising prices reflect government’s economic mismanagement: Congress
points: AICC General Secretary In-charge of Communication, Publicity and Media, Jairam Ramesh.

Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh cited a survey which found that, for 61% of families across the country, monthly household expenditure had risen by more than 20% over the past year.
While 74% of respondents were cutting back on non-essential spending, 50% had reduced purchases of essential goods, he said.
Citing the survey, Mr. Ramesh said prices of ghee and edible oils had risen by 75%, vegetables by 73%, cereals by 71%, milk and dairy products by 65%, and pulses by 62%.
He also claimed that 200 garment factories had shut down in Noida over the past year, citing the impact of U.S. tariffs, high input costs, and government apathy.
“People’s plates are shrinking, and factories are being locked down.
Yet, the Prime Minister’s only concern remains politics,” he said on X, accusing the government of failing to acknowledge people’s hardships or offer relief.

items.title: Digital data the equivalent of 3.2 lakh pages of archival documents handed over
points: Noor Microfilm International Centre handing over 3.2 lakh digital images of the Gazettes of the Hyderabad Government to the Telangana State Archives and Research Institute as a part of the third phase of the digitisation and conservation of archival documents.

Digital data, the equivalent of 3,20,598 pages of Persian and Urdu and English Gazettes of historical significance were given to the Telangana State Archives and Research institute as part of the third phase of handover of digitised records.
The move is a part of an agreement of the Microfilm International Centre and the TSARI.
According to Zareena Parveen, Director, TSARI, this marks a handover of digital data which covers as many 5,22,171 pages.

Touching upon the importance of the documents, she said that these are of great value for researchers and scholars pursuing studies on the political, administrative, cultural and socio-economic history of Hyderabad State and the Deccan region.
Ali Akber Niromand, Regional Director, NMIC, stated that the digital images had been prepared to international standards of storage.

items.title: Police recover all the jewellery stolen from Tanishq showroom in Madurai
points: Rajendiran looking at the recovered ornaments in the city on Tuesday (November 17, 2026). | Photo Credit: G.
Moorthy All the 11.384 kg of gold and diamond ornaments, stolen from Tanishq showroom in Madurai, have been recovered intact, Commissioner of Madurai City Police S.

items.title: Video: Speeding Bus Runs Over Group Helping Intoxicated Man On Punjab Road
points: A group of people who had stopped to assist a young man lying on a road in an intoxicated state were run over by a speeding college bus in Punjab's Ludhiana district on Sunday.
A video of the incident has since gone viral on social media.
In the video, some men can be seen standing with their two-wheelers on Ludhiana's Machhiwara-Kuhara road, trying to talk to the man lying on the road and attempting to move him to a safer location.
Suddenly, a yellow bus came from behind and ran them over.
Kirandeep Singh, who was injured in the accident, said that he was on his way to Machhiwara to get his car repaired.
Upon seeing a young man on a scooter lying on the road in an intoxicated state, he, along with others, including a man referred to as 'Khalsa Ji ', stopped to help.
They were in the process of moving the man off the road toward a nearby petrol pump.

points: The Press Council of India’s (PCI) guidelines on reporting in conflict zones have recommended that governments not invoke stringent laws such as UAPA, NSA or sedition against journalists for their reports, a suggestion on which the council’s chairperson…

items.title: Assam: 2 tenants held for murdering retired OIL employee, wife, daughter
points: A retired Oil India Limited (OIL) employee, his wife and their only daughter were found dead inside their home in Assam’s Dibrugarh on Monday, police said on Tuesday.
Police arrested two persons in connection with the murders, who were tenants in the same house.
The deceased have been identified as Chandrakanta Bhuyan, 64, his wife Eliza Bhuyan, 55, and their daughter Niharika Bhuyan, 28.
Dibyajyoti Dutta, officer-in-charge of Duliajan police station, said police received information about the alleged murders on Monday afternoon and rushed to the house.
The two accused, Raju Das, 27, a resident of Duliajan, and Amir Das, 27, of Borahi Nagaon village in Charaideo district, were arrested from the Avadh Assam Express on Tuesday.
“As per the footage, they had entered the house at around 8am but the recording stopped at around 11am.
They left the house nearly one and a half hours later, so we suspect that the murders were committed between 11am and 12pm,” Dutta told HT on Tuesday afternoon.

items.title: GRAP Stage III restrictions revoked in Delhi-NCR as AQI improves to 204
points: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) on Tuesday lifted Stage III restrictions under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) across Delhi-NCR, citing a sustained improvement in air quality over the past three days.
Delhi recorded a daily average Air Quality Index (AQI) of 204 on Tuesday, prompting the pollution watchdog to withdraw the additional curbs.
The latest AQI reading marks a considerable improvement from the levels exceeding 400 that Delhi recorded in the aftermath of Diwali.
Announcing the withdrawal in a post on social media platform X, the CAQM said: "CAQM Sub-Committee on GRAP decides to revoke GRAP Stage III as daily AQI shows a downward trend, reaching 204 today.
The decision brings some relief to residents and businesses in Delhi-NCR, where tighter pollution-control measures had been in place since November 6.

items.title: Iran Embassy Threatens 2 US Navy Officers It Blames For Minab School Strike
points: Iran’s embassy in South Africa threatened the two senior officers of the destroyer USS Spruance the same day the ship returned to San Diego after a 357-day deployment.
The embassy had accused the same two officers in an earlier post in March of ordering missile launches that hit a school in Minab and killed 168 children.
Iran says the strike on the Minab school took place on February 28, and the Pentagon has not yet released the findings of its own investigation.
The US Navy said the destroyer launched some of the first Tomahawk missiles into Iran on February 28 when the United States and Israel began Operation Epic Fury.
The Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer left San Diego on November 21 last year and covered about 88,000 nautical miles during the deployment.
According to the Navy, USS Spruance spent months in the 5th Fleet area to support the counter-Iran mission after operating in the northern and southern Pacific.

It ordered Banerjee to reply to the show-cause notice within 15 days from the date of its issuance.

points: American Heritage cruise ship crew members have filed a federal lawsuit against the owner and the management company of the tanker that struck the cruise ship in New Orleans on November 13, 2026.
Four crew members of the paddlewheel cruise ship filed the lawsuit in the Eastern District of Louisiana.

items.title: JSW Motors Set To Enter India With Combat SUV
points: GaadiWaadi - The new brand’s first offering will be a rugged-looking plug-in hybrid based on the Chery Jetour T2 The Indian car market is about to welcome another manufacturer, and this time it is a familiar name from the world of steel and infrastructure.

Its first product will be a five-seat SUV called the Combat, which is based on the Chery Jetour T2 sold in international markets.

items.title: Telangana CM seeks Chhattisgarh NOC for Sammakka Sagar project
points: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy on Tuesday met his Chhattisgarh counterpart, Vishnu Deo Sai, in Raipur and sought a No Objection Certificate (NOC) for the Sammakka Sagar project on the Godavari river.

“Responding positively to the request, Vishnu Deo Sai assured the Telangana delegation that the NOC process would be completed at the earliest,” an official statement from the Telangana chief minister’s office (CMO) said.

Revanth Reddy, accompanied by state irrigation minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy, urged Sai to permit water storage in the Sammakka Sagar barrage and sought Chhattisgarh’s cooperation in securing the remaining statutory clearances for the project.
The project was initially proposed at Kantalapalli, where an estimated 11,408 acres of land in Chhattisgarh was likely to be submerged.

items.title: Oil Tanker Hits Malaysian Seawall With 10 Thai Seafarers, Police Believe Unauthorised Sea Trial
points: An oil tanker hit a seawall at Taman Esplanade Marina Wing in Perak, Malaysia, during what police say was likely an unauthorised sea trial.

A joint inspection by the Royal Malaysia Police, the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency and other agencies found that 10 Thai crew members were aboard during the crash, but no injuries were reported.
Citing preliminary investigations, Manjung District Police Chief told reporters that the oil tanker departed for sea trials without permission on the night of November 15, Sunday.
Photos and videos shared on social media platforms appeared to show the vessel’s bow wedged against rocks beside the seawall.
The crash also damaged a section of the sidewalk and nearby public facilities, according to the New Straits Times.
The Police Chief further added that the tanker was previously registered as Fuji.
A recent change in ownership was suspected, as the vessel is now registered in Thailand as Midas.
Following the incident, the Marine Department plans to tow the vessel offshore and anchor it during high tide.

points: The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel deployment at airports is likely to come down as the government is bringing in private security staff to take over non-armed duties, sources have told NDTV.

items.title: India Aims For Top 5 Shipbuilding Rank By 2047 With 4.5 Million Gross Tonnes Capacity
points: India is seeking nearly USD 10 billion in investment to build greenfield shipbuilding clusters and establish itself as a global shipbuilding hub, the Indian Shipping Minister said.
Five new clusters are being proposed along the coast of Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Odisha and Tamil Nadu.
India aims to rank among the top 10 shipbuilding nations by 2030 and the top five by 2047.
The Indian minister for ports, shipping and waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, said that a package of about USD 10 billion is being targeted to develop shipbuilding in India.
An ANI report said the five proposed clusters will be located in Dugarajapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, Kuchhadi in Gujarat, Kendrapada in Odisha, Dighi in Maharashtra, and Thoothkudi in Tamil Nadu.

At the India Shipbuilding Investment Conclave 2026, Sonowal discussed India’s growing maritime ventures and said domestic demand is for more than 400 ships, with an active order pipeline of over 150 vessels worth more than USD 1.7 billion.
He added that over 80% of the order value is from exports.

points: NITI Aayog, the government’s public policy think tank, on Tuesday held a national workshop titled “Leadership as a Mission” in New Delhi on governance lessons from Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 25 years in public office.
“The role of strong political and administrative leadership is crucial in driving India’s development journey.

items.title: Melina Travlou: IMO Must Listen to the Shipping Industry and Pursue a Realistic, Globally Balanced Decarbonisation Framework
points: Two months after the latest round of negotiations at the IMO on reducing greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from international shipping ended without an outcome, and ahead of their critical resumption, there are no signs of any meaningful progress.

It is disappointing to witness such a marked lack of political consistency on the part of the European Union on an issue of such major importance.

items.title: Ola Says Its Own Battery Cells Will Cost 20% Less. But Will This Help Its Scooters?
points: Ola Electric believes making battery cells at its own factory could eventually give it a cost advantage of about 20% compared with buying cells from outside suppliers.
This is a future cost target, not a saving Ola has already demonstrated across its entire scooter range.
Nor does it mean an Ola scooter will suddenly become 20% cheaper.
Buying cells from specialist suppliers keeps the carmaker or scooter maker away from the enormous cost and complexity of cell production.
It says it has commissioned a total of 6 GWh of annual cell-manufacturing capacity at its gigafactory, after adding a further 3.5 GWh.

If cells represent 30% of a vehicle's manufacturing cost, reducing the cell cost by 20% would lower the overall vehicle manufacturing cost by roughly 6%, before allowing for any extra factory expenses.
A battery pack also needs a case, thermal protection, electronics, wiring and safety systems; none of these becomes 20% cheaper merely because the cells do.
